doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Moving to swing: Marian McPartland, Hackett and McKenna
summary: After Storyville he stayed with swing: McPartland trio, Hickory House, Maynard Ferguson, Bobby Hackett at Condon's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well you eventually went and played with Marian.

Yeah. Well I went into Swing music forever. I never went back to the bebop thing. Never went back to it, I never went back, no. I went out with Marian, right after that I went with her trio, for years. I was in the Hickory House for years with Toshiko you know. I was with Maynard Ferguson at Birdland and things like that. Once I got with these guys, that was it. That was it. I headed for John Bunch and Count Basie, playing with Count in a little combos you know, oh, Dave McKenna, and after Marian I went right with Bobby Hackett. They hired me when we were in Ohio. He says, “Get back to New York and you come over and work at Condon’s with us. It’ll pay way more.” And anyway, to work with McKenna, you know, beautiful. Then we added Bob Wilber and Cutty Cutshall and we went out and we always had that good quartet, you know.
Well do you know what it was about your playing that they liked?
Don’t know. Don’t care as long as they hired me.
No, no, no, no, no don’t analyze it at all, no not at all.
